title: One land behind, three Plains ahead in hand
deckReference: Michael Loconto — Pro Tour New York 1996
era: 1996 Standard representative play using current trigger wording
story: My Plains was the only land I controlled when my opponent untapped their two Island s. On my next upkeep, Land Tax saw their two lands against my one and triggered. Neither land count changed before resolution. I searched for three basic Plains, revealed them, put them into my hand, and shuffled. None entered the battlefield. Later in my main phase, I played my one land for the turn, then kept Swords to Plowshares ready for a creature. We now had two lands apiece, so another Tax trigger was not guaranteed on my following upkeep.
review: 1 Plains versus 2 Islands at beginning of upkeep and resolution permits 3 basic Plains to hand. Later one regular land play makes land counts equal. No extra land play; deck contains Swords to Plowshares.
